intervals.label: design phase
intervals.locator: CLIC Conceptual Design Report vol. 2, arXiv:1202.5940 (first posted 26 February 2012)
intervals.note: Start = the posting of the CDR volume on physics and detectors; earlier CLIC design work is not recorded. The Project Implementation Plan (2018/2019) states CLIC is "under development by international collaborations hosted by CERN". The CERN page and the plan give a schedule of construction "by 2026" and first beams "by 2035"; the CERN page still reads so on 2026-10-26 and no source consulted reports a construction decision, so the schedule is not recorded as intervals.
intervals.quote: This report describes the physics potential and experiments at a future multi-TeV e+e- collider based on the Compact Linear Collider (CLIC) technology.

name: Compact Linear Collider
notes: The Atlas marker is the CERN Meyrin campus, the host laboratory named by the design report; the CLIC site would be 11 to 50 km long depending on the stage and has no exact location in the sources consulted.
The CERN CLIC page says the collaboration comprises "more than 70 institutes in more than 30 countries".

cms_energy.note: The maximum of the three stages is recorded.
cms_energy.quote: CLIC is foreseen to be built and operated in stages, at centre-of-mass energies of 380 GeV, 1.5 TeV and 3 TeV, for a site length ranging between 11 km and 50 km.

length.note: The maximum site length (3 TeV stage) is recorded.
length.quote: CLIC is foreseen to be built and operated in stages, at centre-of-mass energies of 380 GeV, 1.5 TeV and 3 TeV, for a site length ranging between 11 km and 50 km.

summary.plain: A proposed linear electron-positron collider designed as an addition to CERN's accelerator complex, to be built in three stages from 380 GeV up to 3 TeV. Its design is developed by an international collaboration of more than 70 institutes. It is not approved.
summary.technical: CLIC: proposed normal-conducting two-beam-acceleration linear e+e- collider (12 GHz structures powered by a drive beam), staged at 380 GeV, 1.5 TeV and 3 TeV, site length 11-50 km, hosted by CERN. CDR 2012, Project Implementation Plan 2018 (CERN-2018-010-M). The first stage was costed at about 6 billion CHF with ~170 MW (PIP abstract). No approval is recorded in the sources consulted.
